title: Choose the visual world for Before The Heat
question: Bolder hand: foreign forms at full commitment, each mapped onto glassblowing. The dealt leader is the Colorant Roster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Colorant Roster
options.lineage: Character-goods catalogue: a ranked cast of rounded characters with name plates and one-line personality notes
options.thesis: Every colorant is a character with a name plate and a temperament (strikes, devitrifies, toxic), so you pick colour by getting to know it.
options.viewport: A soft-ground shell with tabs. The rod slice sits in the centre. On the right, a roster of colorant cells: a rounded chip, name plate, one-line note ('Gold Ruby: shy until reheated, then strikes'), and its ribbon. Toxic colorants are flagged in their notes.
options.risk: Cute can undercut a serious craft tool, and personality notes must stay strictly factual or they break accuracy.

raised.raise: Destructive actions (Delete, Overwrite, Clear) stand alone, set apart by deliberate empty space.
In the plan, each step's length is its real working time, so the sheet shows where the heat time goes.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software manual: milk-acetate leaves hinged over full-strength coloured divider boards, stepped tab rail
options.thesis: Clear leaves over a colour board work like casing over glass. Each section is a hue, and every panel is a translucent leaf over it.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the right edge: Murrini (oxide orange), Vessel (teal), Plan (ultramarine), Learn (grass), Saved (sienna). The current board fills the ground, panels are milk-acetate leaves over it, and the rod slice sits on the top leaf. Selected states show as a punched hole and errors as a vermilion slip.
options.case: It beats the leader on both axes. Glassblowers know the layering of clear over colour from casing, and the tab rail gives the whole app one clear map.
options.risk: Full-strength section boards fight the glass colours; the alpha of each leaf has to be tuned to keep colorants reading true.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.lineage: A glass spectrogram on a viewing box: charcoal continuum, needle-thin wavelength lines
options.thesis: Every colorant shown by its spectrum: state carried by line form, not hue, so nothing depends on colour alone.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail holds every destination as a tick; the open one (Murrini) blooms into a plate. The slice is matted in graphite and the colorant list is drawn as spectral lines (cobalt's absorption bands, neodymium's sharp lines). Live state is solid, pending is dashed, and a warning is a doubled line.
options.case: Best accessibility discipline and real glass science, since colorants do have spectra. It loses on identification: a spectrogram reads as lab, not hot shop.
options.risk: Spectra need sourcing per colorant or they become decoration; the dark ground drifts toward the current look.

options.label: Shop J-Card
options.lineage: A mixtape j-card: ballpoint on lined inlay stock, side A / side B timed to fit the tape
options.thesis: The plan is written like a mixtape inlay, timed to fit your hot-shop slot: side A prep, side B on the pipe.
options.viewport: Ruled white stock with a red brand stripe. The slice sits on the front flap, and steps run as ballpoint tracks with right-aligned times that must fit a 3-hour slot. Tentative steps are in pencil grey.
options.case: Glassblowers do scrawl shop plans by hand, and timing against a booked slot is real. Clarity drops in the editor, where handwriting slows scanning.
options.risk: Hand-lettered type hurts legibility in dense controls; it must stay confined to the plan.

options.label: Dark Console
options.lineage: Dark-first developer console with hairline seams
options.thesis: Graphite panels with hairline seams and syntax accents.
options.case: It loses both axes: it is effectively today's look.
options.kept: Destructive actions set apart by empty space.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.lineage: Dance notation: a vertical staff where block length is exact duration
options.thesis: The build as a score for gaffer and assistant.
options.viewport: Gaffer and assistant columns flank a centre staff, with time running upward.
options.case: It loses both axes: notation literacy is too high a bar, and the editor has no place in a score.
options.kept: Step length equals real working time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark pro creative tool, like the canvas apps people already use, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A left tool rail with icons, a centre canvas, and a right inspector with collapsible sections.
canonCard.risk: It reads like every design tool, which is close to the current look.
